title: 2018_PMC6013082_Strategic_Response_to_an_Outbreak_of_Circulating_Vaccine-Derived
ehr_evidence: Data were derived from acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) case surveillance, stool specimen testing, administrative vaccination coverage records, and postcampaign monitoring surveys.
summary: Descriptive report of a circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2) outbreak in Syria (2017–2018), detailing case epidemiology, surveillance performance, and the impact of monovalent OPV type 2 vaccination campaigns and environmental surveillance on interrupting transmission.
key_findings: 74 cVDPV2 cases were identified, with a median age of 15 months.
30 cases (41%) occurred in children who had never received an OPV dose.
71 cases (96%) were reported from Deir-ez-Zor governorate.
Environmental sewage sampling and mOPV2 vaccination campaigns successfully interrupted cVDPV2 transmission.
population: children in Syria, primarily aged <5 years
limitations: subnational gaps in AFP surveillance performance
delays in receiving laboratory results due to transport and security constraints
administrative coverage denominators may not reflect actual population due to migration
postcampaign monitoring relies on parental recall
